sheets.title: A finger above 900px — 1366 × 1024
sheets.caption: These two are meant to match, and that is the claim being evidenced. A tablet in landscape gets the wide arrangement — no top bar, so the status strip is the whole of the chrome — and rebuilding the phone's chrome had no business touching it. Twice in this branch it did. `@media (pointer: coarse), (max-width: 900px) { display: none }` hid the strip, whose only replacement is the top bar, which is off above 900px: rail, and nothing else. And the 44px floor this file already carried was deleted as dead code, because below 900px the strip is hidden — but that rule was two conditions and only one had died. Both are restored, and `verify:mobile` now walks a finger across this width; without the fix its tablet stop fails 8 checks.

sheets.title: Portrait tablet — 1024 × 768
sheets.caption: Same arrangement, same floor, same as main. 53px of chrome on a 768px screen is 7%.

sheets.title: A mouse is untouched — 1280 × 800
sheets.caption: Captured with a real mouse, which is what the pointer rule reads. The strip keeps its compact 28px keys and its 40px height, exactly as on main — the floor above applies to a finger and to nothing else.
